orders.failureBehavior: Failure remains a failed proof with labeled evidence; it does not promote capability or authorize bypassing independence.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: No critical-path gate in the supplied table names WO-146 as a prerequisite. Its bounded contribution is operator-launched harness substitution, consistent with the-core-bet: the existing compiled role and lifecycle can have another occupant. It does not supply the resident, source-change transport or independent runtime verification gates; those are explicit non-goals. NoOp retains the two existing harnesses and leaves the Cost line's stated hand translation and uncertainty about Copilot reading the existing hook registration. The supplied records do not count the incidence or duration of that manual work, so its opportunity cost and any acceleration of a selected gate are unknown. The product lead's intended experience is clear; the showrunner should treat this as bounded enabling work, not claim a critical-path gate has been cleared by adding a third harness.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance / fixes that fail: one hook registration, at-most-once handler invocation and compatibility fixtures address competing controls; observed availability labels avoid promising enforcement the host lacks. Tragedy of the commons: scripted-launch and retry bounds account for finite probes, but shared role text is paid by existing harness sessions too, and credit limits do not quantify total interactive or recurring context cost. Drift to low performance: criterion 5 retains the live-denial-plus-fixture standard; raising a cold-start ceiling records acceptance, not evidence of improved efficiency. Escalation: using four existing suites, no new gate and bounded qualification limits procedural growth; the added profile still creates maintenance work whose recurring cost is unknown. Success to the successful: another occupant of the same loadout preserves a credible harness alternative without forking the role system; criteria 4 and 6 preserve the existing choices and separate harness from model identity. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: the intended removal is repeated hand translation, while operator-started qualification and fresh verifier sessions remain explicit costs; recurring rescue reduction is not measured. Rule beating: live episodes and fixtures test the actual lifecycle, but freshness of a session alone does not exclude the cross-session memory channel expressly named in criterion 11. Seeking the wrong goal: reusable role delivery serves operator flow; harness count, green fixtures and receipt volume cannot substitute for saved supervision or progress on the selected product outcome. The supplied trap series report no reopening candidate, and their many nulls establish neither success nor failure.
orders.removalBalance: The Cost line names removals: manual role-procedure translation and uncertainty about how the installed third CLI interacts with existing hooks. It also names a profile entry, probe mode, event-log reader, fixture work, shared cold-start text, generated residue and live qualification. It does not establish that the removals are larger. The supplied WO-146 cost row records elapsedMs=37639592, attempts=5 and machineryShare=0.0663632060623824; tokens, costUsd and gateMs are null, with no comparable measured savings. The supplied verifier-ceiling acceptance additionally records 974 added bytes and a measured 21055-byte cold start. These are real costs, not an observed failure or a basis for inventing a return on investment. For the UIFA engineer and devops roles, reusing one loadout and existing suites is a coherent interface extension that avoids a separate role implementation; its net economy remains unknown.
orders.failureBehavior: The contract generally preserves the previous operating route: criterion 4 retains Claude and Codex behavior, criterion 2 marks unobserved refusal support unavailable, criterion 7 makes missing usage data unknown with a cause rather than blocking, and criterion 9 turns an incomplete qualification episode into a finding within the retry bound. Criteria 5, 8 and 11 label unavailable or untested guarantees and retain qualified harnesses for final review and release close. Existing authority and ownership refusals remain intentional boundaries, not new fallback failures. This supports the intended degradation to existing behavior; the supplied subject contains no live malfunction evidence that would justify claiming the implementation actually demonstrated every fallback. For the UIFA tester, fresh-session qualification is useful evidence with the declared memory limitation, not proof of mechanical independence.

findings.reason: The planned removal is qualitative while shared cold-start growth and an elapsed-cost record are present. Neither a named critical-path dependency nor measured recurring savings establishes that this harness extension removes more cost than it adds. This is an unresolved economy claim, not a structural hold for unknown cost.
findings.reopenWhen: Observed routine Copilot episodes show that the additional translation or rescue work persists after qualification, or observed recurring context and maintenance costs exceed the manual work removed; alternatively, a recorded selected critical-path delay is caused by maintaining this optional harness.

findings.reason: Criterion 9 calls for a fresh independent verifier, while criterion 11 explicitly names CLI cross-session memory as a channel for implementer context and excludes mechanical independence. A new session can therefore satisfy the launch procedure without establishing a blinded judgment. No supplied observation shows that contamination occurred; the constructible case is not a hold.
findings.reopenWhen: An observed fresh verifier context or session-memory record contains implementer narrative, the planted-defect answer or the repair conclusion from another episode before the verifier independently inspects and judges the subject.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: none. WO-145 is in no row of the critical-path table and unblocks no order; the goal standard itself says the adaptive Tinkerer mechanics keep candidate scope. It is sequenced after WO-056 and directly before WO-090, the order that shortens the cold start this order lengthens. NoOp cost in the records: none. No supplied observation or Cost-line figure records a loss from the support's absence; NoOp leaves the candidate a candidate and costs nothing measured. The case for acting is the operator's dated direction (2026-09-11 and 2026-09-19) as the Cost line reports it; this review cannot see that direction and takes the citation as the subject's claim.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: the objective lets the experiment target 'a recurring repository step' while the non-goals forbid exploration outside the order and any authority the order lacks; one of the two must give (finding). Commons: up to 900 s per trial order is 17% of WO-055's whole elapsed time and 15% of WO-137's, and the operator must choose two trial orders; machineryShare is already 0.50 to 0.58 in three of five metered orders (finding). Drift: no decision rule is fixed before the trials, so any of the three outcomes can be read from three records (finding). Escalation: accepted improvements either land inside an unrelated order's diff or become new follow-ups, so process begets process either way; one more paragraph of executor text arrives one order before WO-090 removes text. Success to the successful: low; the support is optional and byte-identical when off, the best NoOp guarantee in the five orders. Shifting the burden: criterion 4 waits on the operator's choice of trial orders, and nothing unequips the support after the third trial (finding). Rule beating: a declined record satisfies a trial, and criteria 2 and 3 disagree on whether a declined record is even admissible (finding); the effect is measured once by the actor who proposed it. Wrong goal: 'seconds, tokens or commands' is a proxy; tokens and commandsRun are null in all five metered rows, so seconds alone will carry the verdict (finding).
orders.removalBalance: No, by the order's own words: 'Names no removal in advance.' The additions are a paragraph of executor text while equipped, one record kind in the decisions generator (permanent, with two refusal conditions), and up to 900 s per trial order. The subject reports a dated operator acceptance for cost without removal; this review cannot see it and does not dispute it. The absence of a removal answers question 3 in the negative; it is not an observed failure or a vision contradiction and is not a hold. Whether any removal appears is the experiment's question, and the design is small and noisy for answering it (findings). Order wall-clock and tokens are unknown.
orders.failureBehavior: Yes when off: criterion 1 makes every role's text byte-identical with the support unequipped, so withdrawal restores the old behavior exactly. Partly when on. The 900 s budget has no enforcer (the non-goals exclude a gate, schedule or hook), so an overrun is only recorded. The one hard mechanism refuses rather than degrades: the decisions generator rejects an experiment record without a measured cost or an effect command, so an executor with no counter, or an honest decline, can fail the host order's decisions check. That check would then stop an order for the sake of an optional experiment.

findings.reason: Criteria 2 and 3 disagree about a declined record. Criterion 3 accepts one experiment record 'run or declined'. Criterion 2 has the generator refuse a record 'without a measured cost or with an effect that names no command'. A declined experiment has neither. Either the generator refuses the record criterion 3 allows, so an honest decline fails the host order's decisions check, or declined records are exempt, and declining becomes the free way to complete all three trials with no information gained.
findings.reopenWhen: The generator refuses a declined record; or all three trial records are declined; or a run record is accepted with a zero or placeholder cost.

findings.reason: The instrument is coarse for the question. Each trial is one unrepeated measurement with no control, taken by the actor who proposed the change. Two of the three units the objective names are not recorded today: tokens and commandsRun are null in all five metered rows. Seconds remain, against run-to-run spreads like the 303 to 1,178 s range WO-142's Cost line gives for one gate. A saving smaller than that spread cannot be told from noise, and three such numbers are to decide whether the support stays equipped. WO-140 is sequenced earlier and may supply counters; that is unknown.
findings.reopenWhen: A trial record claims a saving smaller than the observed spread of the command it measured; or verification re-runs the named command and does not reproduce the effect; or trial records carry null tokens and commands.

findings.reason: No decision rule is fixed before the trials, and no removal is named. The title says 'the record decides whether it stays equipped', but nothing states in advance what record means keep, default or withdraw; WO-138 in the same pass pre-registers its floors. With three records and no threshold, any of the three decisions can be read from any result. The Cost line says plainly that it names no removal and rests on a dated operator acceptance that this review cannot see.
findings.reopenWhen: The planning pass that decides cites no threshold written before the first trial; or the support is kept or made default while the summed measured cost of the trials exceeds the summed measured saving.

findings.reason: The order closes before its question is answered and cannot close without the operator. Criterion 4 needs 'the two further trial orders the operator chose', so the executor cannot satisfy it alone. Two of three trials then happen inside other orders, and the answer arrives at 'the next planning pass'. Nothing unequips the support after the third trial, so an optional cost can become a standing one with no owner.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-145 waits in execution or final review for the operator's choice of trial orders; or the support is still equipped on an order after the third trial with no recorded planning decision.

findings.reason: Objective and non-goals pull apart on scope. The objective allows an experiment on 'a recurring repository step'; the non-goals forbid 'exploration outside the order being executed' and 'any authority an order does not already carry'. An accepted improvement to a gate step or script, made inside a trial order, lands in that order's diff outside its contract, and that order's verifier must judge machinery it was not given. If accepted improvements are only recorded and not landed, each becomes a new follow-up. The mission thesis bars flow from silently authorizing scope expansion; here it is recorded, not silent, so this is a known issue and not a contradiction.
findings.reopenWhen: A trial order's diff touches a file outside its declared surfaces with an experiment record as the reason; or a verification finding is filed against experiment residue.

findings.reason: The 900 s budget is large against observed orders and has no enforcer. It equals 17% of WO-055's whole elapsed time (5,288,212 ms) and 15% of WO-137's (5,875,968 ms), and machineryShare is already 0.50 to 0.58 in three of five metered orders. The non-goals exclude a gate, schedule or hook, so the cap is policed only by the executor that spends it. Criterion 5 records the cold-start total; no criterion records a budget overrun.
findings.reopenWhen: A trial record's measured cost exceeds 900 s; or a trial order's elapsed time or machineryShare rises against these rows with the experiment as the recorded cause.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Same 'deferred' row as WO-084; unblocks no gate; sequence entry 40. NoOp in the records: the guide stands at 1,772 lines on 2026-09-19 against 804 at the 2026-09-08 sweep, so every role's directed reads have grown; the per-role directed-load totals are not recorded and will be measured at activation. The supplied cost table adds context: five cold-start ceiling acceptances in two days (reviewer to 20,480, release-close to 12,288 and then 16,384, verifier to 20,480, executor to 24,576), each raising a ceiling rather than trimming. The drift-to-low-performance observation shows coldStartBytes null for every metered order, so the meter does not see that series. Cost row null.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: every process order in this pass writes more into product 07 (WO-141 criterion 5, WO-135 criterion 5, WO-139 criterion 5, WO-142 criterion 6) while this order trims the guide once; with no ratchet the local goals undo one another (finding 1). Tragedy of the commons: this is the one order that returns shared context; its amount is unmeasured until activation. Drift: the guide more than doubled in eleven days and five ceilings were raised in two; the order improves a standard once and sets none going forward. Escalation: adds no step, check, hook or receipt. Success to the successful: not material. Shifting the burden: none added. Rule beating: directed-load can fall by relocation while what a role actually reads is unchanged, or a relocated rule is simply not read when needed; bytesReadIntoContext is null in every row, so the intended effect is unobservable today (finding 2). Seeking the wrong goal: the title says shorter cold start, the non-goals exclude the generated role text, and the recorded ceiling breaches are all in generated role text (finding 3). Criterion 1's guard that no generated cold-start bytes rise is a floor, not a reduction.
orders.removalBalance: Addition: pointers only; no step, check, hook or receipt. Removal: context bytes from every role's directed reads, amount unknown until criterion 1 measures it. Any positive measured reduction exceeds the addition, so the line's shape is right; its size is unknown, and it is a one-time cut against a guide that grew by 968 lines in eleven days.
orders.failureBehavior: There is no runtime mechanism to fail: the order moves paragraphs and leaves pointers, drops no rule and adds no refusal. If criterion 1 cannot be met for some role the order does not close and the guide stays as it is, which is the old behaviour. The risk is silent rather than refusing: a relocated sandbox-approval or model-specific paragraph that a role no longer meets, which is the predecessor's 'vanished when needed most' failure in miniature.

findings.reason: Criterion 1 is a single before-and-after comparison. The guide grew from 804 to 1,772 lines in eleven days, and four orders in this pass add to product 07. Nothing in the order stops the total returning to its old value, so the removal is one-time against a recurring addition.
findings.reopenWhen: By the next planning receipt after WO-090 closes, the guide's line count or any role's directed-load total is back at or above its pre-WO-090 measurement.

findings.reason: The relocation table accounts for where each paragraph went, not for whether the role that needs it still reaches it. Directed-load falls when a paragraph moves behind a pointer; the actual bytes read may not fall (the role follows the pointer) or the rule may go unread at the moment it matters. bytesReadIntoContext is null in every supplied row, so neither effect is visible.
findings.reopenWhen: A post-WO-090 review, journal or operator correction records a sandbox-approval or model-specific error that a relocated paragraph covered; or bytesReadIntoContext, once populated, does not fall for the roles whose directed-load fell.

findings.reason: The recorded context pressure is in the generated role text: five ceiling acceptances on 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-18 for installed CLAUDE.md plus role skill, two of which defer efficiency changes to 'a later pass'. WO-090 is titled shorter cold start and lists reducing the generated role text as a non-goal. No order in this pass owns that later pass.
findings.reopenWhen: Another cold-start acceptance raises any role's ceiling after WO-090 closes, or the later pass that the 2026-09-18 acceptances defer efficiency to is still unallocated at the next receipt.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Adds a local actor option to gate R. NoOp leaves inspection dependent on existing transports; no comparative cost or quality baseline is supplied.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: implements the existing transport contract. Commons: local compute has real but unmeasured cost. Drift: envelope validity does not imply model quality. Escalation: inspection-only scope limits expansion. Success to the successful: creates a credible non-remote alternative. Intervenor burden: typed availability avoids setup rescue. Rule beating: live results and doubles remain distinct. Wrong goal: interchangeable actors, not model novelty.
orders.removalBalance: Unknown: no larger removal is declared; this is a bounded extension of an existing port.
orders.failureBehavior: Yes: endpoint unavailability becomes typed unavailability and resident NoOp. It does not silently substitute another actor or authority.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate R's first unattended mission proof, also required by WO-111 and WO-117. NoOp leaves unattended drift without this scheduled check; cost is unmeasured.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: a global hold can conflict with independent work. Commons: recurring model checks consume budget. Drift: contract and thesis evidence define drift. Escalation: holds can require follow-up verification. Success to the successful: unavailable verifiers must remain distinguishable from wrong work. Intervenor burden: early detection competes with hold clearance. Rule beating: findings need evidence references. Wrong goal: useful authorized progress, not universal verifier availability.
orders.removalBalance: Unknown: the legacy line does not compare recurring checks with avoided supervision.
orders.failureBehavior: No: unavailable verification yields unknown and holds; drift holds every unattended dispatch. This deliberately fails closed rather than retaining prior dispatch behavior.

findings.reason: An unavailable verifier can stop all unattended work, including work unrelated to the uncertain episode. Whether that scope improves flow while preserving authority remains unobserved.
findings.reopenWhen: Verifier unavailability blocks an otherwise authorized independent order and requires operator rescue without evidence that the order is affected by drift.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate S integration support removes second-lane handwork. NoOp retains an eight-step checklist and the recorded variation across sibling integrations.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: regenerates shared projections consistently. Commons: one command reduces repeated diagnosis. Drift: retained checkpoints and stashes preserve recovery. Escalation: no lifecycle events or automatic acceptance are added. Success to the successful: authored conflicts remain explicit judgments. Intervenor burden: removes remembered integration steps. Rule beating: printed checks are not passing evidence. Wrong goal: integration completion rather than helper activity.
orders.removalBalance: A larger procedural removal is named. The observed review-duration medians are associations, not a demonstrated seven-minute causal saving.
orders.failureBehavior: Precondition failures leave the tree unchanged. Authored conflicts remain recoverable through retained stash/checkpoint state and explicit resolution; the helper does not guess.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate S enables export, repository configuration and WO-120. NoOp retains the recorded repeated document roots and eleven ad hoc root derivations.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: one resolver prevents root disagreement. Commons: shared configuration reduces repeated context. Drift: default-output equality protects current users. Escalation: registration semantics stay separate. Success to the successful: external layouts become possible. Intervenor burden: avoids per-script relocation fixes. Rule beating: alternate-root lifecycle fixtures prove portability. Wrong goal: externalizable control-plane behavior.
orders.removalBalance: The architectural removal is explicit, but its time/context value is not measured in the legacy Cost line.
orders.failureBehavior: Yes: absent configuration reproduces today's layout. Malformed explicit configuration refuses rather than silently writing into an unintended root.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: none directly. Gate R lists WO-110 (the local-model transport); no row or typed prerequisite names WO-138, and WO-111 and WO-118 do not wait on it. It informs a catalog decision for the local actor kind. WO-110 is sequenced before it and its title already has the local transport join the catalog for the inspection profile, so admission precedes qualification (finding). NoOp cost in the records: none measured. NoOp leaves the local kind inspection-only with no measured floor; nothing in the supplied observations or the Cost line records a loss from that. The order's own spend is at least 38 live episodes across two models if each extra cell is one episode, a 30-minute operator session, a permanent evaluation harness and its tests inside npm test. Its dependency WO-137 is metered: 5,875,968 ms elapsed, 3 attempts.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: an activation condition lives in an acceptance criterion instead of a typed edge, so the graph WO-043 and WO-135 built cannot enforce it (finding). Commons: 30 minutes of operator attention for the T2 ranking, remote-model spend for half the episodes (tokens and costUsd are null in every metered row, so unknown), and harness tests added to every later gate; gateStepCount was falling, 76 to 66 (finding). Drift: five repeats of one input per cell cannot support a reliability floor; 5 of 5 is compatible with a true rate near 55% (finding); accepting that as 'qualified' sets a low bar for every later qualification. Escalation: the outcome names 'what the next qualification must show', so the pilot's product is partly another pilot. Success to the successful: one remote comparator and one local build; the non-goals exclude a second remote model, which is reasonable for cost and limits what 'compared' means. Shifting the burden: the held-out ranking is a one-time, recorded operator cost; acceptable if it stays one-time. Rule beating: floors are 'as written at activation' and absent from the judged subject; one-factor cells have no stated repeats (findings). Wrong goal: local roles serve the vision's privacy and model-swap theses, yet criterion 1 qualifies no role that reads private material, so the roles it can admit are the ones where local inference matters least; T3's journal input strains the public-material rule (finding).
orders.removalBalance: No in cost terms. The named removal is an assumption ('local episodes stay inspection-only indefinitely, and its opposite'), not a recurring cost, and the order cannot remove it: all three tasks are read-only inspection tasks, and criterion 4 and the non-goals forbid qualifying implementation or verification. What it can deliver is a measured floor for inspection roles. The additions are concrete and partly permanent: an evaluation harness with tests inside npm test, an evidence directory, at least 38 live episodes and up to 30 operator minutes. The information may still be worth more than it costs; that is unknown until run and is not a hold.
orders.failureBehavior: Yes. Live runs never enter npm test; an episode that fails leaves a typed failure; a blocked pilot reports `inconclusive` with the blocker; nothing in the packet promotes a level. Failure therefore leaves the catalog where WO-110 left it. Two edges: the harness's deterministic tests run inside npm test, so a defect in them refuses every later gate rather than degrading; and if criterion 1's first clause proves false after activation the order has no defined state to return to, because the condition is not a typed dependency.

findings.reason: An activation condition is written as an acceptance criterion. 'The order is not activated otherwise' depends on the outcome row in WO-137's execution record. WO-043's title says only an unmet hard dependency or a planning deferral blocks activation, and WO-135's title has the sequence checked against every typed hard edge. A condition on another order's outcome, in prose inside a criterion, is invisible to both, and acceptance criteria are judged after execution, when the condition can no longer prevent anything.
findings.reopenWhen: Status offers WO-138 for activation while WO-137's record has no successful live inference row; or the executor finds the first clause of criterion 1 false after activation and has no defined state to return the order to.

findings.reason: T3's input strains the public-material rule and the clean-room floor. T3 classifies hook-journal rows; criterion 1 requires every episode input to be committed public material or the seeded scratch repository, and the same input goes to a remote transport for comparison. Hook journals are session records. WO-142's non-goals in this same pass list 'a home-path screen for reports' and 'the absolute store path in the worker prompt' as not addressed, so absolute local paths are known to occur in neighboring material and no screen is named. To satisfy criterion 1 the labeled T3 sample must be committed, which could place journal rows with local paths, session ids or command text in the public tree and in a remote model's input; to avoid that, T3 must read uncommitted rows, which breaks criterion 1. What the journal rows actually contain is unknown from the subject.
findings.reopenWhen: The committed T3 sample or any recorded envelope contains an absolute home path, user name, host name, session id or other local identifier; or a T3 episode reads journal rows that are not in the committed tree.

findings.reason: The design cannot support 'at what reliability'. The budget is three tasks by two models by five repeats: five repeats of one input per cell. Five successes in five supports, at 95% one-sided confidence, a true rate no lower than about 55% (0.05 to the power one fifth is 0.549), and the schema-valid rate moves in 20-point steps. Each task has a single instance (one receipt, one seeded repository, one labeled sample), so variation across inputs, which is what a role meets in use, is unmeasured. The title's 'representative' rests on one case per task.
findings.reopenWhen: The packet states a reliability figure with no n or interval; or a role admitted as `ready` fails its schema or oracle check on a second input of the same task.

findings.reason: The floors that decide the outcome are not in the judged subject. The outcome is `ready`, `negative` or `inconclusive` 'against the floors as written at activation'. This review cannot judge whether `ready` will mean anything. Nothing requires the floors to be fixed before any episode runs or by someone other than the executor who runs them, and WO-137 has already produced live inference rows, so the local model's behavior is partly known when the floors are written.
findings.reopenWhen: The commit that writes the floors is later than the first recorded baseline envelope; or the packet's floors differ from the activation text.

findings.reason: The one-factor cells have no stated repeats. The baseline measures variability across five repeats; 'five one-factor cells' reads as one episode each. A single-episode delta cannot be separated from the repeat variability the baseline itself measures, so 'how much does one prompt or support change move it' may be answered with noise.
findings.reopenWhen: A one-factor delta is reported as an effect while lying inside the baseline's five-repeat range for the same task and model.

findings.reason: A pilot's harness becomes permanent gate load with no named consumer. The deterministic tests over recorded envelopes run inside npm test, so every later order pays them. gateStepCount has been falling (76 at WO-139 to 66 at WO-137). The non-goals make the pilot one-shot (no leaderboard, no second remote model), and the platform lens asks that a capability arrive as an interface something else consumes; the next consumer of this harness is not named.
findings.reopenWhen: gateStepCount rises with WO-138 and no order filed after it names the evaluation harness as an input.

findings.reason: Admission precedes qualification. WO-110 is sequenced before WO-138 and its title already has the local transport 'join the actor catalog for the inspection profile'. WO-138 then decides which inspection roles the local kind may fill. For a `negative` or `inconclusive` role the write-backs name only 'the local kind's qualified roles, dated'; no write-back restricts what WO-110 already offered.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-138 reports `negative` or `inconclusive` for a role while the catalog entry WO-110 shipped still offers the local kind for that inspection role with no recorded restriction.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate S enables target lifecycle, profiles and cross-repository workstreams. NoOp leaves repository identity and authority implicit; costs are unmeasured.

Escalation: no publishing machinery is added. Success to the successful: absent metadata preserves self-repository operation. Intervenor burden: reduces target-selection ambiguity. Rule beating: an authority profile cannot silently grant effects. Wrong goal: usable multi-repository work.
orders.removalBalance: Unknown: the legacy Cost line does not quantify the addition or removed manual interpretation.
orders.failureBehavior: Absent Repository metadata preserves self behavior. Unknown repositories and malformed authority refuse before activation, preventing work against the wrong target.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: none. WO-150 appears in no row of the supplied critical-path table (A, B, C2, C1, R, D, U, S, E, F, G, H, V, P, deferred) and is a blocking prerequisite of no order in the typed graph. The supplied sequence places it after WO-071 and before WO-147, ahead of WO-120 (Gate B) and WO-100 (Gate R). Its stated benefit is executor economy: one paragraph of role text that lets the executor run at most one experiment per order, plus removal of the explicit per-trial equip step. That is a mission-level capability under the operator-flow passage (moving recurring procedure into machinery), not a gate. The goal standard says prerequisite or risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables; the order names none. This review confers no reorder authority; placement is the showrunner's, so the gap is a finding, not a hold. NoOp cost in the records: not quantified. If nothing changes the support stays opt-in, each trial equips it explicitly, and the equip ambiguity the cost line cites (WO-099 D008: the third trial ran unequipped) can recur. The five supplied cost rows (WO-090, WO-110, WO-099, WO-079, WO-069) carry no metric for experiment time, adopted-method savings or equipment state; tokens, costUsd, codeDiffBytes and coldStartBytes are null in every row, and WO-145's own row is metrics: null. The three per-iteration savings the cost line cites (58.7 s, 238.4 s, 0.21 s with one command removed) come from WO-145 and WO-099 decision records that are not in the supplied subject, so they are the order's claim, not this review's observation. The cost line itself says it names no new saving in advance. Net: the record shows neither the cost of inaction nor the measured benefit of action; both are unknown here and are left unknown, which the output instructions say is never a structural hold.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: WO-090 (v0.35.1) shortened the executor cold start; WO-150 adds 1,173 bytes back to every default dispatch, and the cold-start ceiling (the guard) is paired with a standing route that pre-commits to raising it by 4 KB on breach, so the guard cannot bind against this addition. The supplied policy-resistance trap shows guardRefusals 1 (WO-090), 0 (WO-069), null elsewhere, no worsening; nothing observed, but the two mechanisms undo each other by construction. Tragedy of the commons: the cost line accounts the per-dispatch addition (1,173 bytes; at most 900 s per order) but no horizon total. The supplied sequence lists roughly sixty orders after WO-150; each non-opted-out executor dispatch carries the bytes and may spend the 900 s. Operator attention is also consumed by each ceiling-breach acceptance. No criterion measures experiment time; per-order token accounting is a declared non-goal. Drift to low performance: the supplied drift trap is already reopenCandidate true with gateStepCount worsening 65, 72, 73, 74, 80 across the five rows, and its coldStartBytes and subjectCharacters indicators are null (unmeasured). WO-150 feeds the third indicator by default and, through criterion 2's 'never trimmed around', commits to moving the standard rather than meeting it. The standard stays explicit, which is better than none, but the supplied acceptances show it moved seven times in four days across four roles (executor 24,576; verifier 20,480 then 25,151; reviewer 20,480 then 24,576; release-close 12,288 then 16,384). Escalation: a projected 249-byte margin (about 1% of 24,576) after shared rules that added 865 and 974 bytes at a time makes the next shared reviewed rule a near-certain breach, which provokes another dated acceptance. The cold start rose from 20,849 (2026-09-18 acceptance) to 22,174 (v0.33.2, WO-145 D003 as cited) to 23,154 (2026-09-21, after a shortening order) if those are the same measure; that is an inference from the subject's own numbers, labeled as such. Success to the successful: the default flip is decided by a pre-registered rule and an operator acceptance, not by investment, which is the right shape.
